mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month triggers a term premium compression, reducing expected equity discount rates and thereby pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) during the same FEDFUNDS regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations, which elevates risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the month before the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 5,000 jobs over three consecutive months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which elevates equity risk appetite and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥5,000 each month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified labor expansion window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by more than 10% in a month compared to the prior month, it reflects sudden demand weakness, which compresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the same month's regime.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3 points signals softening manufacturing capacity, which raises uncertainty and elevates the cost of capital, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥3 points in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising UNRATE above 4% (average) indicate wage growth pressures that, when sustained, increase the real wage premium and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the wage growth episode.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST rises by at least 8% in a month, it suggests a surge in retail activity that, if continued, lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥8% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the observed retail expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 4-month declining trend in GDPC1 (real private consumption) combined with FEDFUNDS < 4% suggests a shift to contractionary policy and a term premium expansion, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows a 4-month negative trend AND FEDFUNDS < 4% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p < 0.05) during the contractionary regime.
